STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: Three reproduced failures: a gzip response under `Compress(ETag(h))` shares its ETag with the identity body, a HEAD with no body gets a validator from the empty body, and headers set after the first Write behave differently from unwrapped net/http. Streaming, controller passthrough, ServeContent, Recoverer, and concurrency held up.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files deleted; `git status` is unchanged: ` M README.md`, `A middleware/etag.go`, `A middleware/etag_test.go`)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Compress outside ETag gives a gzip body with the identity-body ETag. An identity client presenting that tag gets 304. Repro: `Compress(5)(ETag(leaf))`, leaf sets `Content-Type: text/plain`. Gzip response: `CE="gzip" ETag="\"71a0f557…\""`. Identity request with that If-None-Match: `code=304`. Strong tags must differ per content-coding. The ETag-outer order is fine.
- [blocking] HEAD handler that writes nothing and sets no Content-Length gets `ETag="\"e3b0c442…\""` (the empty-body hash). GET on the same handler gets `"e1c4f457…"`. This is the triggered "HEAD never carries a validator from an empty body" check, failing.
- [blocking] Differential, not on the approved list. Handler writes `<html>x</html>`, then sets `X-Late=1` and `Content-Type: application/x-custom`. Real server, direct: `X-Late=""`, `CT="text/html; charset=utf-8"`. Wrapped: `X-Late="1"`, `CT="application/x-custom"`. Net/http ignores headers set after the first write; the wrapper honours them.
- [minor] GET 200 with handler-set `Content-Length: 10` and no body gets no ETag (`code=200 ETag=""`). Criterion 2 says GET gets one. The HEAD exemption in criterion 6 was applied to GET too.
- [minor] Panic after a buffered write under an outer recover-and-swallow middleware loses the body: `code=200 body=""` (not reproduced against the unwrapped version, which should send "partial").

CHECKS:
- `Compress(ETag)` and `ETag(Compress)` on a real server, identity and gzip clients → Compress-outer fails (above), ETag-outer passes.
- HEAD no-body probe → fail (above).
- Late-header differential on real server → fail (above).
- Flush streaming on real server: "part1" reached the client before the handler resumed → pass, but see OPEN QUESTIONS.
- `http.NewResponseController`: SetWriteDeadline, Flush through the wrapper, and Hijack after a write (raw wire = status line, headers, RAW) → pass.
- ServeContent with handler ETag: match → 304 empty body; no match → 200 "abcdef"; FileServer GET 200, HEAD with `If-None-Match: *` → 304 → pass.
- chi Recoverer outermost, handler panics after write → 500 "oops", no ETag → pass. Recoverer inside ETag → 200 "partial…" → pass.
- 32 goroutines × 20 requests, real server, `-race` → pass.
- obs-text tag `"\xff\xc3\xa9"` matches itself; DEL byte `"\x7f"` does not match → pass.
- `etagMatches` 200k random byte inputs (no panic) and 5000 constructed `"zz", W/"<etagc>" ,"yy"` lists → pass. My first generator used DEL/space, which aren't etagc, so those failures were my error.
- Read the table tests for unquoted, unterminated, `W/` alone, empty value, `*` in a list, and comma-in-quotes: they assert the right outcomes.
- Sibling Flush/Hijack/Push error strings match compress.go's wording. README row and link present.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- The APPROVED DIFFERENCE "Flush must not send bytes before the response completes" contradicts criterion 9, which requires Flush to commit buffered status, headers and body. The code follows criterion 9, and "part1" streams early. Which wording is correct? If the approved difference stands, Flush fails it.
- Is the header-after-write behaviour (finding 3) intended? If yes, it needs to go on the approved list.
